title: Sinop & Amasra: Quiet Western Black Sea Coastal Route
seoTitle: Sinop & Amasra Coastal Route Guide | Itinerary of Türkiye
metaDescription: Plan a quiet Western Black Sea road trip from Safranbolu to Amasra and Sinop. Fortress prison, Hamsilos Bay, driving times, and best swim months.
quickAnswer: A Sinop and Amasra coastal road trip links two compact Black Sea peninsulas along Türkiye's forested northern shore. Starting from Safranbolu, drivers reach Amasra in 1.5 hours (95 km) and continue east via the scenic D010 highway to Sinop in 5.5 to 6.5 hours (320 km), ideally between late June and September.
category: Inner Pages — 20 Boutique Destination Guides (ITO 52-Destination Hub)

body.text: Travellers looking for salt air without resort crowds often overlook the western Black Sea. Where the Aegean and Mediterranean fill with summer charter flights, the stretch between Amasra and Sinop keeps a slower maritime cadence. Independent planning with [Itinerary of Türkiye](https://itineraryofturkiye.com/) lets you pace this route around weather windows, local seafood seasons, and quiet harbors rather than fixed coach schedules.
Why is Sinop's peninsula considered one of the calmest Black Sea towns?

Sinop sits on the narrow Boztepe promontory, where geography naturally slows traffic and limits urban sprawl. As the Black Sea's only natural sheltered port, the town faces south toward calm water, avoids heavy transit highways, and has repeatedly been ranked Türkiye's happiest province by the Turkish Statistical Institute ([Go Türkiye](https://goturkiye.com/sinop/see)).

Because the main east–west Black Sea highway bypasses the peninsula to the south, Sinop never absorbs through-truck traffic. Residents walk between the fishing wharf, tea gardens, and small ship-model workshops that still carve miniature wooden vessels by hand. Ancient Miletian settlers founded the colony in the 7th century BCE, and the third-century BCE philosopher Diogenes the Cynic was born here ([Go Türkiye](https://goturkiye.com/cruising/sinop-port)). Today, that self-contained layout makes Sinop easy to explore on foot without constant traffic noise.
What historical landmarks (Sinop Fortress Prison, Hamsilos Fjord) stand out?

Sinop's two defining stops pair stark Ottoman-era architecture with rare coastal geology. Inside the peninsula's defensive walls sits the Historic Sinop Prison, nicknamed the "Alcatraz of Anatolia" before closing in 1999 to become a museum ([Go Türkiye](https://goturkiye.com/sinop/see)). Fourteen kilometers northwest, Hamsilos Nature Park preserves a narrow, river-like sea inlet framed by dense pine forest.

Both Sinop Fortress and Amasra Fortress appear on Türkiye's 2026 [UNESCO Tentative List](https://whc.unesco.org/en/tentativelists/7030/) as part of the Genoese Maritime Network stretching from the Mediterranean to the Black Sea. Inside Sinop's citadel, stone cellblocks date to 1887 and once held prominent Turkish writers including Sabahattin Ali ([Türkiye Museums](https://turkiyemuseums.com/en/museums/sinop-historic-sinop-prison)). Out on the İnceburun peninsula, Hamsilos Bay is commonly called a fjord, though geologists classify it as a ria—a drowned river valley where calm sea water cuts inland beside Akliman Bay ([Go Türkiye](https://goturkiye.com/sinop/see)). In Amasra, walk across the Roman-era Kemere Bridge connecting Zindan Castle and Sormagir Castle, then visit the compact Amasra Archaeology Museum.
How do you drive from Safranbolu to Amasra and Sinop?

Driving from Safranbolu to Amasra takes roughly 90 minutes (95 km) via Bartın on well-paved dual carriageway. Continuing from Amasra to Sinop along the coastal D010 highway covers 320 km and requires 5.5 to 6.5 hours of focused driving because of continuous switchbacks, coastal villages, and steep forested headlands between Cide and İnebolu.

Splitting the coastal leg with an overnight stop in Amasra—or a lunch break in İnebolu—prevents driver fatigue. Avoid driving the Cide–Abana–Ayancık section after dark, as mist rolls off the sea quickly and livestock occasionally cross blind bends. Travellers pairing western Anatolia with northern heritage routes often start from [Bursa](https://itineraryofturkiye.com/destinations/bursa) before heading northeast to Safranbolu.

body.text: Which months are warm enough for the Black Sea?

Late June through early September is the reliable window for swimming in Amasra and Sinop. During July and August, daytime air temperatures average 26°C to 29°C and Black Sea surface water reaches 23°C to 25°C, offering refreshing relief compared with southern Türkiye's 38°C summer heat.

May and early June bring lush green hillsides and quiet waterfront tables, though sea temperatures remain brisk around 17°C to 20°C. October turns the coastal beech forests amber and brings fresh Black Sea anchovies (hamsi) and bonito (palamut) to harbor grills, making autumn ideal for food-focused road trips even after beach weather ends. For cold-season alternatives elsewhere in the country, see our [winter travel guide to Türkiye](https://itineraryofturkiye.com/blog/turkey-in-winter-premium-travel-guide).

faq.q: How many days do you need for Amasra and Sinop?
faq.a: Plan 4 to 5 days from Safranbolu: one night in Amasra, one slow coastal driving day with a stop in İnebolu or Cide, and two nights in Sinop to cover the Historic Prison, Hamsilos Bay, İnceburun Lighthouse, and Erfelek Tatlıca Waterfalls.

faq.q: Can you fly directly to Sinop instead of driving from Amasra?
faq.a: Yes. Sinop Airport (NOP) operates scheduled domestic flights from Istanbul, sitting roughly 8 km from town. Flying into Sinop works well if you prefer a short one-way car rental back toward Kastamonu or Ankara.

faq.q: Is the D010 coastal highway safe for standard rental cars?
faq.a: Yes, the D010 is fully paved and suitable for standard sedans. The challenge is curvature rather than surface quality: maintain moderate speeds, use engine braking on steep descents, and complete the drive in daylight.

faq.q: What local dishes should you order in Amasra and Sinop?
faq.a: In Amasra, order Amasra salatası (a colorful seasonal salad of more than twenty finely cut herbs and vegetables) alongside freshly fried red mullet or whiting. In Sinop, try walnut-topped Sinop mantısı (hand-folded dumplings) and flaky nokul pastry.

faq.q: Is Hamsilos Bay suitable for swimming?
faq.a: The sheltered inner inlet is mostly admired from wooden walkways and forest trails, while nearby Akliman Bay and Karakum Beach on Sinop's peninsula offer broader sandy stretches for swimming.

faq.q: Are Amasra and Sinop crowded in August?
faq.a: Amasra draws heavy weekend traffic from Ankara and Istanbul in July and August, so visiting Tuesday through Thursday is noticeably quieter. Sinop remains calmer year-round because of its greater distance from major cities.
